species.size: 5 inches spike to spike; peelers 3 inches; mature adult females exempt
species.limit: 1 bushel per person per 24 hours; 2 bushels per boat with more than one person
species.quote: Crabs must not be less than 5 inches from spike to spike across the back, except peelers, which must measure at least 3 inches, and mature adult females. Recreational crabbers may take no more than one bushel of crabs during any 24-hour period; on a boat with more than one person, no more than two bushels. No sponge (egg-bearing) crabs are allowed.
species.notes: Up to six crab traps (2 x 2 ft or smaller) with two 2⅜ in escape rings and a lime/fluorescent green float marked with name and address.

species.zone: Georgia state waters (cast net, food shrimp)
species.season: Food-shrimp cast netting follows the commercial season, generally mid-June through mid-January; bait shrimp (4 quarts/day) has no closed season
species.limit: 48 quarts heads-on or 30 quarts tails per person per day
species.quote: A person may not possess more than 48 quarts of heads-on shrimp or 30 quarts of shrimp tails in any day. Recreational cast netters are limited to two quarts per person at any time and may take a maximum of four quarts of bait shrimp per day; there is no closed season for the harvest of bait shrimp.
species.notes: Georgia fishing license and free Saltwater Information Permit (SIP) required. Exact opening/closing dates are set by Coastal Resources Division each year.

species.season: Open year-round by law (check CRD seasonal closures; summer harvest is usually closed)
species.limit: 2 bushels per person per day; 6 bushels per boat per day
species.quote: Oysters must measure no less than three inches from hinge to mouth. Up to two bushels of oysters and one bushel of clams per person per day; a maximum limit of six bushels of oysters and one bushel of clams per boat per day.
species.notes: Georgia fishing license and Saltwater Information Permit required. Harvest only from approved public harvest areas (CRD maps).

species.season: Open year-round by law (check CRD seasonal closures)
species.limit: 1 bushel per person per day; 1 bushel per boat per day
species.quote: The maximum depth from one shell half to the other must be at least ¾ inch thick. Up to two bushels of oysters and one bushel of clams per person per day; a maximum limit of six bushels of oysters and one bushel of clams per boat per day.
species.notes: Georgia fishing license and Saltwater Information Permit required.

species.limit: See federal regulations
species.quote: Billfish (Blue marlin, White marlin, Sailfish)* | Billfish may be landed in Georgia, provided the angler complies with all federal regulations. Visit CoastalGaDNR.org/HMS for federal regulations.
species.notes: Georgia prints no state season, size or bag; defers entirely to federal HMS rules. CoastalGaDNR.org/HMS links to https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/topic/atlantic-highly-migratory-species/overview

species.season: All year (printed in the shark block with 'Sharks (other than Hammerheads, SSC and Prohibited Sharks)' — 1 per angler or boat, whichever is less)
species.limit: 1 per angler or boat, whichever is less
species.quote: Hammerhead Sharks (Great, Scalloped, and Smooth)A | 78 FL
species.notes: Printed as a sub-row of the Sharks block; the limit column is merged with the 'Sharks (other than ...)' row above it. Footnote A: also federally managed — see NOAA HMS. Sharks: hook and line only; non-offset, corrodible, non-stainless circle hooks required except with flies/artificial lures. Must be landed with head and fins intact.

species.limit: NO HARVEST
species.quote: Prohibited Sharks (NO HARVEST)A | Sand tiger, Sandbar, Silky, Bigeye sand tiger, Whale, Basking, White, Dusky, Bignose, Galapagos, Night, Reef, Narrowtooth, Caribbean sharpnose, Smalltail, Atlantic angel, Longfin mako, Bigeye thresher, Sharpnose sevengill, Bluntnose sixgill, Oceanic Whitetip, and Bigeye sixgill

species.size: 12 inches total length statewide (lake exceptions: 14 in at Blackshear, Lanier, Oconee, Walter F. George, West Point, PFA lakes; no minimum at Blue Ridge, Burton, Juliette; Lindsay Grace protected slot 15–22)
species.limit: 10 (counts in the 10 black bass daily limit, Game Species Daily Limits page); 5 on Public Fishing Areas
species.quote: Largemouth Bass 12 inches statewide except: Lake Blackshear: 14 inches Lake Blue Ridge: no minimum (0 inches) Lake Burton: no minimum (0 inches) Lake Juliette: no minimum (0 inches) Lake Lanier: 14 inches Lake Oconee: 14 inches Lake Lindsay Grace: bass between 15 and 22 inches must be released immediately. All others may be kept. In addition, only one bass may be greater than 22 inches. Lake Walter F. George: 14 inches West Point Reservoir: 14 inches Public Fishing Area lakes operated by the Department of Natural Resources: 14 inches.
species.notes: Bag from Game Species Daily Limits: 'All black bass species (Genus Micropterus). 10'. PFA page: 'Largemouth bass: 14 inches minimum unless otherwise posted.' and 'Largemouth bass (unless otherwise posted) - 5'. Per-PFA exceptions: Marben 'five (5) largemouth bass, only one (1) of which can be 16 inches or longer'; Dodge County 'between 16 and 24 inches must be released immediately ... (limit 5 total per person, only 1 over 24 inches)'; Evans County 'between 12 and 16 inches must be released immediately ... Limit five (5) per person, with only one (1) over 16 inches'; Hugh M. Gillis 'between 16 and 24 inches must be released immediately ... (limit 5 per person)'; Ocmulgee 'Largemouth bass are catch-and-release'; Paradise '5 total per person, only one over 24 inches'; Silver Lake Panic Pond 'one fish greater than 24 inches per day'.

GA–SC border: 'White bass | All border waters covered except for Savannah River downstream of Clarks Hill dam | 10 | No size limit'; 'Striped bass, hybrid bass, white bass or combination | Savannah River downstream of Clarks Hill dam | 2 | 27-inch minimum length limit'. species.season: Possession prohibited on Public Fishing Areas
species.limit: Must be released immediately (PFAs)
species.quote: Grass carp must be released immediately.
species.notes: Printed only in the Public Fishing Areas length/daily limits block; no statewide limit is printed.

species.limit: 1 bushel per person
species.quote: Whelk (conch) Recreational harvest of whelk is limited to 1 bushel/person. There is no minimum size, closed season or closed area. A recreational fishing license and Saltwater Information Permit (SIP) are required, including hand harvest from the beach.
species.notes: Bushel = 8 gallons (recreational fishing page definitions). Not printed on the gadnrle.org shrimpregs page — eRegulations guide only.

species.size: None (recommended: claw at least 2 3/4 inches elbow to tip of immovable finger)
species.limit: No limit
species.quote: Georgia does not regulate the harvest of stone crab; however, the harvest of the whole crab is discouraged. It is recommended that only one claw measuring at least 2 3⁄4 inches from the elbow to the tip of the lower, immovable finger be removed. A properly removed claw should not have meat from the body attached.
species.notes: Unregulated; the agency prints a recommendation only (one claw, 2 3/4 inch minimum, no body meat attached). Same text on the eRegulations shrimp/crab page.

species.limit: 2 quarts per person at any time (licensed saltwater guide: 10 quarts)
species.quote: Bait minnows may be harvested year-round. ... No individual recreationally harvesting bait minnows may possess more than two quarts of bait minnows at any given time. A licensed saltwater fishing guide may possess not more than 10 quarts at any given time.
species.notes: Gear: no more than two minnow traps recreationally (guide: four); trap less than 24x18x9 in or 30 in circumference, throat no larger than 1 in, bar mesh not smaller than 1/4 in, tag/float with name and address; seines and cast nets also allowed year-round.
